bluf: Ukraine's defensive operations are stabilizing the frontline against mounting Russian losses, but the Kremlin remains committed to maximalist war aims including full seizure of Donetsk and Luhansk. Russian nuclear exercises with Belarus and a failure to secure the Power of Siberia-2 energy deal reveal strain in Moscow's strategic posture even as occupation authorities accelerate forced integration of Ukrainian territories.

sections.title: Military Operations
sections.content: Ukrainian forces continue to hold the frontline and have made territorial gains following Russia's loss of access to Starlink in February 2026. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte confirmed on May 21 that Ukraine's defenses are stabilizing the frontline, while the US Defense Intelligence Agency assessed that Ukraine has gained ground. Russia's intensified drone and missile strikes, including a large-scale attack with 546 drones and missiles on May 17-18, have targeted critical infrastructure but failed to break Ukrainian defenses. Ukraine's new domestically produced guided glide bomb will likely expand its battlefield air interdiction capability, and Ukrainian long-range strikes on Russian defense industrial plants and oil infrastructure in Moscow City and Oblast on May 16-17 demonstrate an expanding ability to impose costs on Russia's rear areas.
sources: Ukraine’s Fortress Belt: The Key to Sustaining the Frontline

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.content: Despite mounting elite recognition that the war has reached a 'dead end,' Russian President Vladimir Putin remains committed to fully seizing Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts by end of 2026. Russia and Belarus completed combined nuclear exercises on May 21, deepening de facto control over Belarus and signaling willingness to escalate. Putin's failure to secure the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline deal during his visit to China on May 20 highlights limits on Russo-Sino cooperation, as Beijing exploits Russia's urgent need for alternative energy markets.

sections.title: Occupation Atrocities and Integration
sections.content: Russian occupation authorities are accelerating the forced integration of Ukrainian territories through deportation of children, military-style training for teenagers, and coercive bureaucratic measures. Russian officials are preparing to transfer a child from the Oleshky Boarding School to Russia for medical operations, potentially violating international humanitarian law. Over 80 residents from the boarding school have already been transferred or deported. The Russian Presidential Fund for Cultural Initiatives is spending billions of rubles on cultural integration, while VTB Bank expands influence through savings accounts and occupation officials automate newborn registration into Russian systems.

key_developments: Ukraine's defensive operations are stabilizing the frontline, with NATO and US intelligence confirming territorial gains.
Russia conducted large-scale nuclear exercises with Belarus, signaling readiness to escalate and deepening control over Minsk.
Putin failed to secure the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline deal during his China visit, exposing limits on the Russia-China partnership.
Ukrainian long-range strikes hit the Moscow Oil Refinery and defense industrial sites, demonstrating an expanding reach into Russia's rear.
Russia continues systematic deportation of children and forced integration of occupied Ukrainian territories.
outlook: Ukraine is likely to sustain its defensive line through the summer, but a global shortage of Patriot interceptors and Russian ballistic missile campaigns will pressure air defenses. The Kremlin will likely double down on nuclear coercion and occupation consolidation while seeking to salvage its strategic position through diplomacy with China and pressure on Ukraine's allies.
